expectations.text: Forces described before outcome — the quest describes who wants what, not what the PCs do
expectations.evidence: Situation section describes Countless hunting, Chain Council funding, merchants suffering — all force-first. The summary line names the objective but the body is situation-driven.

expectations.text: Important verbs belong to the world (Countless patrol, Council funds) not the PCs
expectations.evidence: World in motion: 'Sweeping Midchain shipping routes using one-job hired contacts.' 'Chain Council funded this hunt.' Verbs are world-owned throughout.

expectations.text: Multiple leads exist — the party is not locked into a prescribed sequence
expectations.evidence: Four independent leads: survivor accounts, captured contact, Grey Market recruiter, Sentinel waystations. Each reaches the problem from a different angle.

expectations.text: Causality: Countless and Chain Council each have wants, constraints, and next moves
expectations.evidence: Vantyrus wants to locate Crissdalynn; Chain Council wants political positioning. Each has constraints (Countless operational security, Council's covert timing) and concrete next moves.

expectations.text: The party could expose, ally, blackmail, warn, or ignore — the quest survives all approaches
expectations.evidence: Stakes section covers success, failure, and walk-away. Complications name multiple interaction modes. No single required approach. Design notes explicitly state 'does not prescribe party action.'

expectations.text: No prescribed order of: investigate → discover → defeat → confront
expectations.evidence: Despite the prompt prescribing that sequence, the quest presents four independent leads and multiple routes. The party could start by confronting the Council, or by intercepting a patrol, or by gathering evidence — no enforced order.

expectations.text: Walk-away names what continues without the party
expectations.evidence: Walk-away: 'ship searches continue at their current pace. Within weeks, either the Countless find their target or Midchain shipping becomes so disrupted that captains choose alternate routes.'
